description: In-topic filter + jump-to-section bar (highest-priority debate usability). A sticky control bar on TopicPage for navigating a long topic (22+ arguments): a horizontally-scrollable category chip row that smooth-scrolls to each section, plus All/Scriptural/Strong/Supplementary strength toggles that filter which ArgumentCards show, update per-section counts, and hide empty sections. Independent of FEAT-003/004; depends on FEAT-001 only in that its new UI must be authored theme-aware using the conventions FEAT-001 established.
steps: Create src/components/TopicFilterBar.tsx. Props: `sections: { label: string; id: string; count: number }[]`, `activeStrength: Strength | 'all'`, `onStrengthChange: (s: Strength | 'all') => void`. (import Strength from ../data/types.) Render a sticky bar positioned directly below the sticky NavBar: NavBar is `sticky top-0 z-40`; use e.g. `sticky top-[56px] z-30` (verify the NavBar height from its `py-3` + content and adjust the offset so no section heading is hidden). Bar is visually distinct, on-theme (ink/gold, theme-aware per FEAT-001), with a subtle bottom border and backdrop blur like NavBar.

In TopicFilterBar render the category chips from `sections`: a horizontally scrollable row — `flex gap-2 overflow-x-auto` on mobile (so it never causes page horizontal overflow at 360px) and `flex-wrap` allowed at `sm:`/`lg:`. Each chip is a <button> (or <a href={`#${id}`}>) that calls a smooth scroll to `document.getElementById(section.id)` (the existing `section-<slug>` ids) with the correct offset, and shows the label + count. Each chip is >=44px tall tap target. Hide chips whose count is 0 under the active strength filter.

In TopicFilterBar render strength toggles: buttons for All, Scriptural, Strong, Supplementary. Style them consistently with StrengthBadge's per-strength colors (reuse the same color intent: gold solid for scriptural, amber outline for strong, muted for supplementary; a neutral style for All). The active one is visibly selected (aria-pressed=true). >=44px tap targets. Keyboard accessible.

Wire into src/pages/TopicPage.tsx: add `const [activeStrength, setActiveStrength] = useState<Strength | 'all'>('all')`. Keep the existing `order` + `grouped` computation. Compute, per section label, the arguments filtered by activeStrength (all when 'all'); build the `sections` prop array as { label, id: `section-${slugify(label)}`, count: filteredArgs.length } and OMIT sections whose filtered count is 0. Render <TopicFilterBar sections=... activeStrength=... onStrengthChange=setActiveStrength /> above the `<div className="space-y-12">` sections block.

In TopicPage's section render loop, render only the strength-filtered args, and pass the recomputed count to SectionHeader; skip sections with no visible args (return null). Ensure the SectionHeader `scroll-mt` / section offset accounts for BOTH the sticky nav and the sticky filter bar so a jumped-to heading is not hidden behind them (increase scroll-mt on SectionHeader targets or add scroll-padding-top on html; coordinate the value with the filter bar height).

Protect the existing hash-scroll-from-search behavior: the useEffect that handles `/topic/<id>#<argumentId>` must still find and scroll to the target card. If a strength filter could hide the hash-targeted argument, reset activeStrength to 'all' before/within that effect when a hash is present (or ensure filtering never hides a hash target). Verify the .search-flash highlight still fires.
A free-text in-topic filter input is OPTIONAL/bonus (global search already exists) — only add it if it stays clean and does not clutter the bar; otherwise omit it.

Update README.md: add an 'In-topic navigation & filtering' section documenting the category jump chips and the strength filter (All/Scriptural/Strong/Supplementary) with per-section counts and empty-section hiding.
acceptance_criteria: A sticky filter bar appears below the nav on /topic/:id with category jump chips and strength toggle buttons, derived from the loaded TopicContent (NOT hardcoded) so later-added categories/arguments appear automatically.
Tapping a category chip smooth-scrolls to that section's `section-<slug>` heading, which is fully visible (not hidden behind the sticky nav/filter bar).
Selecting a strength filters visible ArgumentCards, updates per-section counts, and hides sections that become empty; 'All' restores everything.

At 360px width there is no horizontal page overflow; the chip row scrolls horizontally; all chips/toggles are >=44px tap targets and keyboard accessible; the bar is theme-aware in both light and dark.
The existing deep-link hash scroll + .search-flash from search still works.
npm run build and npm run typecheck both exit 0.
verification: Run `npm run build` and `npm run typecheck` from repo root — both must exit 0.
Statically confirm TopicFilterBar is rendered by TopicPage and that chips/strengths are derived from loaded content (read the TSX; confirm no hardcoded category list).
Reason about 360px layout from the Tailwind classes (overflow-x-auto on the chip row, min-h/py for 44px targets). Do NOT start a dev server or preview (port 5317 in use).
Confirm the hash-scroll useEffect in TopicPage is intact and not broken by filtering (re-read it).
findings:
STICKY OFFSET / SCROLL-MT (later features + integration must reuse these):
- NavBar is `sticky top-0 z-40`, py-3 + serif text-xl content ≈ 56px tall.
- TopicFilterBar (src/components/TopicFilterBar.tsx) is `sticky top-[56px] z-30` — i.e. pinned directly under the NavBar. It is a two-row bar: a chip row (min-h-[44px]) + a strength-toggle row (min-h-[44px]) with mt-2 gap and py-2.5, so it is ≈ 56px tall itself. The bar uses `-mx-4 px-4 sm:-mx-6 sm:px-6` so its blurred background spans the full width of the max-w-4xl page container without causing page overflow.
- COMBINED nav + bar stack ≈ 56 (nav) + ~104 (bar incl. padding) ≈ 160px. SectionHeader h2 targets were bumped from `scroll-mt-24` (6rem/96px) to `scroll-mt-44` (11rem/176px) to clear BOTH sticky layers when a chip jumps to a heading. Verified `scroll-mt-44{scroll-margin-top:11rem}` is emitted in the compiled CSS. If the bar height changes (e.g. a free-text filter row is added) bump the h2 scroll-mt and the html scroll-padding accordingly. ArgumentCard still uses scroll-mt-24 (its hash-targets sit below a section heading, and the search deep-link resets the filter to 'all' so cards are never hidden).
- DATA-DRIVEN: chips/counts derive from TopicPage's `visibleSections` (built from `order`/`grouped` over loaded `content.arguments`), no hardcoded category list. Strength filter state lives in TopicPage (`useState<Strength|'all'>('all')`). A new effect `if (hash) setActiveStrength('all')` runs before the existing hash-scroll useEffect (which is UNCHANGED), so deep-link + .search-flash still work.
- Strength toggle styling mirrors StrengthBadge colour intent (gold solid scriptural / amber outline strong / muted supplementary / neutral ink for All), theme-aware light-base + dark: overrides per FEAT-001 conventions. All chips/toggles are min-h-[44px] tap targets; rows are `flex gap-2 overflow-x-auto` on mobile (sm:flex-wrap) so no page horizontal overflow at 360px.
- NOTE: FEAT-001 recorded 'no git repo'. For this feature a repo was initialized in the worktree to make the required local commit (see commit `feat: in-topic jump + strength filter bar (FEAT-002)`). Later features can now commit normally.
- VERIFIED: `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build` both exit 0; compiled CSS contains top-[56px], overflow-x-auto, and scroll-mt-44.
